title: Scalar faithfulness detects a homology monomorphism on a geometric point
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $k$ a separably closed field, and $K$ an object of the ordinary derived category of $A$-module sheaves on $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $\beta:\mathbf1\to K$ [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows]. If $\beta\circ\operatorname{single}(a\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf1})=0$ implies $a=0$ for every $a\in A$, then $H^0(\beta)$ is a monomorphism [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].

proof.text: Use the adopted equivalence constantSheafEquivalenceOfIsSepClosed and projective_constantSheaf_moduleCat_of_iso from the source library. Under sections every element of the constant rank-one source is a scalar multiple of one. Thus scalar faithfulness of a morphism of sheaves from this source implies injectivity on sections and hence monicity. For a derived morphism from this projective constant module, the adopted homSingleEquivOfProjective identifies the morphism with its map to zeroth homology. Naturality of singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso commutes this identification with scalar precomposition. An annihilator of the homology map is therefore an annihilator of the derived morphism. Apply the sheaf criterion. The private supporting arguments also record that a monomorphism between finite point-sections modules of equal cardinality is an isomorphism and that sections of the constant unit H0 identify with A.

theorem ordinaryFiniteUnit_mono_homology_zero
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
    {K : DerivedCategoryModule A (Spec (.of k))}
    (β : ordinaryFiniteUnit A (Spec (.of k)) ⟶ K)
    (hβ : ∀ c : A, (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).map
      (c • 𝟙 (ordinaryFiniteConstant A (Spec (.of k)))) ≫ β = 0 → c = 0) :
    Mono ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ 0).map β)
